issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts the estimate with no constant depending on the window. The proof's last step bounds the weighted norm $\|\,|\widehat{\chi_\Omega f}|*|\check g|\,\|_{L^q_{v_s}}$ from the unweighted Young bound using only $\|\check g\|_{L^1}=1$; Young's inequality in the weighted space $L^q_{v_s}$ requires the weighted kernel norm $\|\check g\, v_s\|_{L^1}$, which is strictly larger than 1 in general (and the claimed identity $\|\check g\|_{L^1}=\|\mathscr F g\|_{L^1}=1$ confuses $\mathscr F g$ with $\mathscr F^{-1}g$). Hence the stated constant-free inequality is not established and is false for suitable $f$ and windows.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the constant $C_{g,s}=\|\check g\,v_s\|_{L^1}<\infty$ (finite since $g\in C_c^\infty$) through the lemma and absorb it into the constant $C$ of Proposition prop:supported_approximation_sobolev_space_local and Corollary cor:Barron.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space is unsupported as an exact-constant statement; the downstream uses (prop:supported_approximation_sobolev_space_local, cor:Barron) only need the embedding with some constant, so they survive once the window constant is carried.
issues.title: FL-to-M lemma states a window-independent constant its proof cannot deliver
issues.why_classification: A local bookkeeping fix (insert the finite weighted kernel norm) preserves every substantive claim and guarantee; no rate, class, or advertised scope changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the estimate~\eqref{stima1} can be improved by replacing \(|\Omega + \Omega|^{1/p}\) with \(2^{1/p} |\Omega|^{1/p}\)
for each $\xi\in\rd$, $V_g (\chi_\Omega f)(\cdot, \xi)$ is supported in $\Omega+\Omega$

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed improvement replaces $|\Omega+\Omega|^{1/p}$ by $2^{1/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}$. The proof's observation $|x+y|=2|(x+y)/2|$ only shows the set identity $\Omega+\Omega=2\Omega$ for convex $\Omega$, whose measure is $2^d|\Omega|$, not $2|\Omega|$. The proof mechanism controls the $L^p_x$-norm by the measure of the support of $V_g(\chi_\Omega f)(\cdot,\xi)$, which is contained in $\Omega+\operatorname{supp} g$ of measure up to $2^d|\Omega|$; no argument in the paper yields the factor $2^{1/p}$, and for $d\ge2$ the claimed bound is smaller than what the construction delivers (e.g. $\Omega$ a ball with a window filling it gives the factor $(3/2)^{d/p}>2^{1/p}$).

failure_location.quote: The thesis follows by observing that, for every $x,y\in\Omega$, we can write  \[|x+y|=2|(x+y)/2|=2|z|\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed factor $2^{1/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}$ by the supported one $(2^d|\Omega|)^{1/p}=2^{d/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}$, and delete or weaken accordingly the convex-case statements in prop:supported_approximation_sobolev_space_local and cor:Barron.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space_convex is false as stated, and the convex-case variants asserted in Proposition prop:supported_approximation_sobolev_space_local and Corollary cor:Barron (factors $2C|\Omega|$) become unsupported; the non-convex bounds survive unchanged.
issues.title: False convex-case improvement of the FL-to-M embedding
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained constant correction, but it withdraws the advertised convex-case improvement (and the corresponding claimed constants downstream), so more than a routine edit is lost; the main non-convex guarantees survive, hence not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
In detail,
$$M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}(\rr{d})\hookrightarrow M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+1}}(\rr{d})$$
if and only if $s_1>d/2$ and $s_2>n+1+d/2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only supplies the embedding $M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}\hookrightarrow M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+1}}$, which controls $f$ through $\|f\|_{M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}}$ and hence covers the $Q^{s_2}=M^2_{v_{s_2}}$ branch. The second branch bounds the error by $\|f\|_{L^2_{s_1}}+\|f\|_{\mathscr{F}L^2_{s_2}}$, which would require the inclusion $L^2_{s_1}\cap\mathscr{F}L^2_{s_2}\hookrightarrow M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}$; this inclusion is false in general. Counterexample: for well-separated parameters $(y_k,\omega_k)$ with $\langle y_k\rangle\simeq\langle\omega_k\rangle\simeq k$ and coefficients $c_k=\langle k\rangle^{-\max(s_1,s_2)-(d+1)/2-\varepsilon}$, the sum $f=\sum_k c_k e^{2\pi i\omega_k\cdot x}\psi(x-y_k)$ satisfies $\|f\|_{L^2_{s_1}}+\|\widehat f\|_{L^2_{s_2}}<\infty$ while $\|f\|^2_{M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}}\simeq\sum_k|c_k|^2\langle y_k\rangle^{2s_1}\langle\omega_k\rangle^{2s_2}=\infty$ since $2\min(s_1,s_2)>d$. So the second branch of \eqref{eq:Hilbert_approximation_bound_L} has no supporting argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the second branch to $f\in M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}$ (equivalently drop it, keeping the $Q^{s_2}$ branch), or prove the required embedding, which cannot hold with the stated sharp indices.
issues.overall_effect: The approximation estimate in $\mathscr{F}L^2_{s_2}$-based terms (and the accompanying prose about $L^2_{v_s}$ and $\mathscr{F}L^2_{v_s}$ classes) is unreliable; only the $Q^{s_2}$ branch is supported.
issues.title: Second branch of Shubin/Hilbert corollary is not established
issues.why_classification: A contained fix (restricting the second branch to a modulation-norm class, or proving a lossy inclusion) preserves a recognizably comparable result; only the over-ambitious function class is lost, not the rate or the main guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\bb{D}_\Omega = \{ x \mapsto \sigma\left(\tfrac{\eta\cdot x}{\tau}+b\right)
        \varphi(\tfrac{\eta\cdot x}{\tau}+b-t)\phi(x-y) \text{ such that }(y,\eta, b) \in\Omega\times\rr{d}\times \rr{}\}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof represents $f$ through the STFT inversion formula, which integrates the atom $\rho(x,y,\eta,b)=\sigma(\tfrac{\eta\cdot x}{\tau}+b)\varphi(\tfrac{\eta\cdot x}{\tau}+b-t)\phi(x-y)$ against the density $C_{\sigma,\varphi}\vartheta(\eta,b)V_\phi f(y,\eta)$ over ALL $y\in\rr^d$. The theorem's dictionary $\mathbb{D}_\Omega$ only contains atoms with $y\in\Omega$, so the measure $\mu_f$ is not a measure on the dictionary and the identity $f=\int_{\tilde{\mathbb D}_\Omega} i\,d\mu_f$ does not follow; no argument restricting the representing measure to $\Omega\times\rr^d\times\rr$ is given, and none can hold in general: for $f=T_z\phi$ with $\operatorname{dist}(z,\Omega)=R$ large, every atom is $O(e^{-cR^2})$ on $B(z,1)$ while $f$ is $O(1)$ there, so any representing measure has total variation $\gtrsim e^{cR^2}$, whereas the theorem's right-hand side $C\|f\|_{M^{p,q}_m}$ is (for $s_1=0$, i.e. $p\le1$) independent of $z$. The central representation and variation-norm bound of the proof are therefore unsupported and the stated global $N^{-1/2}$ bound is false as written.

failure_location.quote:
which in turn allows us to represent $f$ in the integral form containing all the required components:
    \[
        f=\int_{\tilde{\bb{D}}_\Omega} i_{\tilde{\bb{D} }_\Omega\rightarrow W^{n,r}(\rrd)} d \mu_f.
    \]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either remove the restriction $y\in\Omega$ from the dictionary (changing the advertised construction) or restrict the target class to functions with prescribed spatial localization near $\Omega$ and reprove the representation, the variation-norm bound, and the uniform dictionary bound for that class.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:approximation_sobolev_space_G, its advertised global $W^{n,r}(\rr d)$ guarantee, and the dependent global corollaries for the Feichtinger algebra (cor:added-2) and potential Sobolev spaces (cor:added-3) are unreliable; the global regime on $\rr d$ as advertised (with shifts restricted to a fixed bounded set) is not established.
issues.title: Global approximation theorem: dictionary restriction breaks the representing measure
issues.why_classification: The central global guarantee (approximation of every $f\in M^{p,q}_m$ on all of $\rr d$ by atoms with shifts confined to a fixed bounded set) cannot survive any repair that keeps the advertised dictionary: translated targets are exponentially hard for this dictionary, so an advertised regime must be excluded and a comparable global guarantee does not survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider  the weight $m =(v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2})$ with $s_1,s_2$ satisfying \eqref{eq:indices}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs the embedding $M^{p,q}_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}\hookrightarrow M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+s}}$ for some $s>1$, which via Theorem thm:embeddings requires $s_2>n+s+d/q'$, i.e. $s_2>n+1+d/q'$ strictly. The theorem instead assumes $s_2$ as in \eqref{eq:indices}, which gives exactly $s_2=n+1$ when $0<q\le1$; then no $s>1$ satisfies $s_2>n+s$, so \eqref{eq:cpq} cannot be justified and the proof fails in the regime $0<q\le1$ (and likewise the integer-value branch used in cor:added-3 for $0<q\le1$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to $s_2>n+1$ (strictly, e.g. $s_2\ge n+1+\delta$ for some $s>1$), or restate Theorem thm:approximation_sobolev_space_G for $q>1$ only.
issues.overall_effect: The global approximation bound is unsupported for $0<q\le1$ under the stated weights; the corollary for potential Sobolev spaces with $0<q\le1$ inherits the gap.
issues.title: Index regime of the global theorem incompatible with its embedding step
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained restatement of the admissible weight range (excluding a boundary regime), leaving a recognizably comparable theorem; but it does exclude part of the advertised index range, so it is more than minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
By the triangle inequality,
\[
\bigl|V_\varphi \sigma(x,\omega)\bigr|
\;\geq\; |T_2(x,\omega)| - |T_1(x,\omega)|
= \frac{1}{2\pi}\,e^{-\pi x^2} - |T_1(x,\omega)|.
\]
This implies the lower bound \eqref{eq:lowerbound}.

If it vanished at any real point $(x_0,\omega_0)$, then by the identity theorem for analytic functions it would vanish on a non-empty open set, and hence on the entire real plane (since the real plane has accumulation points).

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The strict lower bound does not follow: $|V|\ge T_2-|T_1|$ implies $|V|>T_2$ only if $|T_1|<T_2$-small, which is never established and is false — $|T_1|$ is not $o(T_2)$ uniformly. In fact the claim is false: $V_\varphi\sigma(0,\omega)=\int_0^\infty t e^{-\pi t^2}e^{-2\pi i\omega t}\,dt\to0$ as $|\omega|\to\infty$ by the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma, while \eqref{eq:lowerbound} demands $|V_\varphi\sigma(0,\omega)|>\tfrac{1}{2\pi}$ for all $\omega$. (ii) The alternative argument misapplies the identity theorem: a holomorphic function of several complex variables (or even one variable) may vanish at isolated points without vanishing on an open set, so non-vanishing cannot be concluded this way. (The only fact actually needed downstream — existence of one $(t,\tau)$, $\tau\ne0$, with non-zero STFT — follows trivially from Lemma lem:relu-origin and continuity in $\omega$.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the lower bound \eqref{eq:lowerbound} and the identity-theorem argument; establish Condition (A) directly from Lemma lem:relu-origin and continuity of $V_\varphi\sigma$ in $\omega$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated strict lower bound \eqref{eq:lowerbound} is false and its proof invalid; the non-vanishing statement is unproven. Downstream use is unaffected because Condition (A) only needs one non-vanishing point, which holds trivially.
issues.title: False strict lower bound and invalid non-vanishing proof for the ReLU STFT
issues.why_classification: Removing the false bound and replacing the argument by a trivial continuity remark preserves every substantive use (Condition (A)); no rate, class, or guarantee is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Using the classical complex estimate
\[
|\operatorname{erfc}(z)|
\le C\,\frac{e^{-|z|^2}}{1+|z|},
\qquad z\in\cc{},
\]
The estimates above imply that the STFT is in $L^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes 1}(\rr{2})$ which means $\sigma\in M^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes 1}(\rr{})$, for every $s\in\rr{}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The invoked estimate $|\operatorname{erfc}(z)|\le Ce^{-|z|^2}/(1+|z|)$ is false on $\mathbb C$: along the negative real axis $\operatorname{erfc}(-R)\to2$, so no Gaussian decay holds there. With $z=\sqrt\pi(-x+i\omega)$ this fails precisely for $x>0$; indeed at $(x,0)$ the true value $V_\varphi\sigma(x,0)=\int_0^\infty t e^{-\pi(t-x)^2}dt\approx x$ grows linearly, while the claimed bound is $O((1+x)e^{-\pi x^2})\to0$. Hence the corollary's decay estimate is false, and Remark rem:33's conclusion $\sigma\in M^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes1}(\rr{})$ for every $s\in\rr{}$ fails with it (in fact $\sigma=t_+\notin M^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes1}$ for $s\ge-2$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the estimate by the correct sectorial bound (Gaussian decay in the $\omega$-direction and the correct $\operatorname{erfc}$ behavior for $x>0$), restate rem:33 with the corresponding admissible weights, and remove the false intermediate estimate.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:relu-decay is false as stated, and the membership claim $\sigma\in M^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes1}$ for all $s$ in rem:33 collapses with it; the auxiliary decay control in the $x$-direction is overstated. No main theorem depends on these statements.
issues.title: False decay estimate for the ReLU STFT from an invalid complex erfc bound
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of an auxiliary estimate preserves all substantive claims; the false corollary is not used by any labelled result.
